newsitem.title: USA: Confident shoppers to hit stores this holiday.
newsitem.headline: Confident shoppers to hit stores this holiday.

text.p: Would-be Santas are generally feeling merry about the economy, new consumer surveys reported Tuesday, but it's still unclear exactly how generous shoppers plan to be this holiday season.

According to the American Express Retail Index released Tuesday, the average consumer expects to spend a total of $1,160 this year on gifts and entertainment. The figure, based on a survey of 800 shoppers, is about even with the amount consumers expected to spend last year before the holiday shopping season officially began.

Meanwhile, a monthly post-election survey by the Chicago-based retail consulting firm Leo J. Shapiro & Associates reports that more consumers are willing to spend more this holiday season compared with general spending sentiments in October. However, Shapiro added that overall holiday spending plans so far remain below the level seen in November 1995.

"Following the election, when the survey was conducted, there was a tremendous surge in confidence in the nation," Shapiro explained. "There was a sharp increase in the willingness to buy major goods, excluding cars. There was a sense of euphoria that will affect Christmas (buying patterns)."
But it's anyone's guess as to how long that election-inspired consumer confidence will last, Shapiro warned.
"True success at Christmas (for retailers) will depend on whether they will be forced to mark down prices to prop up sales as they did in previous years," Shapiro explained.

Consumer confidence, according the most recent surveys, is playing a major role in how shoppers are preparing for the official start of the holiday shopping season next week, the Friday after Thanksgiving.
The results of the American Express and Leo J. Shapiro surveys jibe with the results of recent consumer spending polls.

Last month, the National Retail Federation and the accounting firm Deloitte & Touche estimated that consumers will spend about $764 for holiday gifts this year, up 11.5 percent from the $685 spent one year ago. A poll by the Gallup Organization, Visa and the trade group International Mass Retail Association also reported that consumers expected to spend $806 this year, a 20 percent increase on 1995 spending levels. A similar poll by MasterCard said the average American will spend $765 on presents this year, unchanged from 1995 figures.

Yet, Uncle Sam is putting a pessimistic spin on the holiday shopping outlook. The Commerce Department last week reported that consumers spent just slightly more in October than they did in September, news that sparked concerns among analysts and retailers that the holiday season might not live up to expectations.

But on the somewhat brighter side, the American Express Retail Index indicates that more people will splurge on a spouse or child this year than in 1995 by spending 21 percent more on that person. Additionally, more than one-third of the shoppers surveyed expect to spend $1,000 or more on gifts in 1996.

Consumers are also watching their shopping dollars a little more this year than in 1995, according to the American Express poll. Ten percent more shoppers are expected to visit discount stores for holiday gifts this year compared with one year ago, and 5 percent plan to visit factory outlet malls this holiday season.

Chain store sales remain slightly above expected levels, according to a weekly snapshot of retail chain store sales conducted by Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi/Schroders. Overall, the BTM/Schroders index anticipates a 3-3.5 percent increase in same-store sales in November.

But some consumers -- along with retailers and analysts -- are concerned about the fact that there are five fewer days of shopping in 1996 vs. 1995. Nearly 30 percent of those surveyed by American Express said they began looking for gifts before Oct. 1. However, a majority (66 percent) plan to wait until after Thanksgiving to begin their Christmas shopping quest in earnest.
